questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Famous chefs and their secret recipes
The scientists who create food flavours
Why chocolate is so popular around the world
How supermarkets keep food fresh for longer
questions.why: Neil says they'll be meeting the flavourists, scientists who create the flavours in our food.

questions.q: According to Sam, what influences flavour besides the tongue?
options: Only the smell of food, nothing else
The price of food and where it's from
How food looks, smells and is described
The temperature of the room you eat in
questions.why: She says flavour is also influenced by how food looks, smells and even how it's described.

questions.q: Why do some scientists think combinations like strawberries and cream work well?
options: Their chemicals overlap in special ways
They are the same colour
They are both sweet
They grow at the same time of year
questions.why: Sam says some scientists think their chemicals overlap in special ways.

questions.q: What was the flavour industry like in the 19th century, according to Dr Nadia Berenstein?
options: It was run by large supermarkets
It was taught at many universities
Recipes were shared openly with everyone
A few firms kept secret family recipes
questions.why: She says a dozen or so companies used secret recipes, sometimes passed from father to son.

questions.q: What increased demand for new flavours after the Second World War?
options: More people eating out in restaurants
Processed food in supermarkets and fridges
New flavour schools opening in Europe
Cheaper sugar from abroad
questions.why: Neil says the invention of processed food sold in supermarkets and kept in fridges increased demand.

questions.q: How do people become flavourists today?
options: By studying flavour science at university
By passing a difficult government exam
By training at work with a master
By working in a restaurant kitchen first
questions.why: Dr Berenstein says there's no academic path; training is on-the-job with a master flavourist.

questions.q: How does Dr Berenstein describe the flavourist's job?
options: Only scientific, with no creativity
Simple and easy to learn
Mainly about business and selling
Scientific but also creative
questions.why: She says 'it's a scientific profession for sure… but it is a creative profession'.

questions.q: Why does Neil compare a flavourist to a magician?
options: They add a little of this and that for taste
Because flavourists perform tricks on stage
Because their recipes are secret and dishonest
Because flavourists work mostly at night
questions.why: He says he loves the idea of adding a pinch of this and a drop of that to create a magical taste.
